summary: Validated photo upload feature end-to-end. Backend: 7/7 new upload tests PASS (POST /api/admin/uploads success, 401 no-auth, 400 non-image, 400 >5MB, webp/gif accepted, GET 404, product persistence with relative URL). Backend regression: 61/61 tests PASS (54 prior + 7 new; test_pakasir_settle.py excluded due to pre-existing ModuleNotFoundError unrelated to this feature). Frontend: PhotoPicker renders both modes; URL mode preview + clear works; Upload mode POSTs to /api/admin/uploads (200 with {url,id,size}); preview displays uploaded image via resolveImageUrl. Storefront ProductCard shows uploaded photo (naturalWidth>0). OrderModal thumb shows uploaded photo. Regression: external URL products still render.

minor.issue: Backend sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable correctly, but ingress (Cloudflare) rewrites it to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on the public URL. Browsers will re-fetch every load, defeating the immutable cache. Verified: localhost:8001 returns immutable header; public URL returns no-store. Not fixable in app code — needs infra/ingress config change.

Pre-existing test file uses 'import server' which fails ModuleNotFoundError when pytest runs from /app root. Not caused by this iteration but blocks full-suite runs. Suggest fixing sys.path or using package import.

issues: Minor a11y warning: DialogContent missing aria-describedby/Description (pre-existing, not from this feature).

action_items: (Optional) Investigate ingress Cache-Control override so uploaded product images can be cached long-term by browsers — either change ingress config or serve images from a subpath the ingress doesn't rewrite.
(Optional) Fix backend/tests/test_pakasir_settle.py import path so full pytest suite can run from /app.
critical_code_review_comments: POST /api/admin/uploads reads full file into memory before size check — an attacker could send a 500MB upload and consume RAM before the 5MB limit rejects it. Consider streaming/reading chunks with an early cutoff OR check Content-Length header first.
Content-Type is trusted from client (`file.content_type`); a malicious client could send an executable with content_type='image/png'. Consider magic-byte sniffing (first bytes) for defense-in-depth.

MongoDB is not ideal for binary blobs at scale — 16MB doc limit per file is fine for 5MB images, but a large catalog will bloat the 'uploads' collection. Consider GridFS or object storage if catalog grows.
server.py now ~1416 lines — split into routers/uploads.py + others is overdue (flagged in iter3 too).
resolveImageUrl handles '/api/' and '/uploads/' — good; passes external http(s) URLs through unchanged (regression-safe).

PhotoPicker exposes rich data-testids (photo-picker, photo-mode-url, photo-mode-upload, pf-photo, pf-photo-file, pf-photo-upload-btn, pf-photo-preview, pf-photo-clear, pf-photo-error) — excellent for automation.
